meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: in full on the day of discharge
facts.summary: Massachusetts: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due in full on the day of discharge.
facts.evidence_quote: any employee discharged from such employment shall be paid in full on the day of his discharge

facts.value: in full on the following regular payday
facts.summary: Massachusetts: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due in full on the following regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: any employee leaving his employment shall be paid in full on the following regular pay day, and, in the absence of a regular pay day, on the following Saturday

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Massachusetts basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 In no case shall the Massachusetts minimum wage rate be less than $0.50 higher than the effective federal minimum rate.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Massachusetts independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): Yes
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.value: An employer or payor of income must complete new hire reporting within 14 days of an employee’s or independent contractor’s effective date of employment or effective date of reinstatement (reinstatement of employment after a lapse in pay of 30 calendar days or more or, for an independent contractor, the date of commencement of employment under a new contract).
facts.summary: Massachusetts new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): An employer or payor of income must complete new hire reporting within 14 days of an employee’s or independent contractor’s effective date of employment or effective date of reinstatement (reinstatement of employment after a lapse in pay of 30 calendar days or more or, for an independent contractor, the date of commencement of employment under a new contract).
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: An employer or payor of income must complete new hire reporting within 14 days of an employee’s or independent contractor’s effective date of employment or effective date of reinstatement (reinstatement of employment after a lapse in pay of 30 calendar days or more or, for an independent contractor, the date of commencement of employment under a new contract).
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Massachusetts: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Weekly; Bi-weekly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 9: Massachusetts. Hourly employees must be paid either weekly or biweekly.  Employers may pay salaried employees semi-monthly.  Note: Salaried employees can also be paid monthly if an employee voluntarily agrees. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Massachusetts is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Massachusetts base new employer UI rate: 2.42%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.
